question.text: Scenario: Fatima is a Non-Resident Indian (NRI) based in Dubai with mutual fund investments across multiple schemes of XYZ Mutual Fund. She decides to redeem some of her investments. The RTA processes the following redemptions: Redemption A: 5,000 units of XYZ Equity Large Cap Fund purchased 18 months ago at NAV Rs.200, redeemed at current NAV Rs.280. (Equity-oriented fund, holding period > 12 months) Redemption B: 3,000 units of XYZ Corporate Bond Fund purchased 10 months ago at NAV Rs.30, redeemed at current NAV Rs.33. (Debt fund, holding period < 36 months for specified mutual fund) Redemption C: 2,000 units of XYZ Balanced Advantage Fund purchased 6 months ago at NAV Rs.150, redeemed at current NAV Rs.162. (Equity-oriented fund, holding period < 12 months) Redemption D: 1,000 units of XYZ Liquid Fund purchased 24 months ago at NAV Rs.1,500, redeemed at current NAV Rs.1,620. (Debt fund, holding period < 36 months) Fatima has submitted her PAN and all KYC documents are in order. The RTA must compute TDS on each redemption. Question 3 of 5: For Redemption C (Balanced Advantage Fund explicitly stated as equity-oriented and held for 6 months), what is the nature of the capital gain and the applicable STCG rate when STT is paid?

answer.text: STCG taxed at 30% since it's a hybrid fund
STCG taxed at 10% as applicable to all balanced funds
STCG taxed at 20% since the Balanced Advantage Fund is equity-oriented and units are held for less than 12 months
LTCG taxed at 12.5% since balanced funds get preferential treatment

explanation.text: The Logic: The scenario explicitly states that Redemption C is from an equity-oriented Balanced Advantage Fund. Per NISM Series X-B, units of equity-oriented mutual funds held for 12 months or less generate Short-Term Capital Gain, and STCG on equity-oriented funds where STT is paid is taxed at 20%. Gain = (162 - 150) x 2,000 = Rs.24,000, so STCG tax at 20% = Rs.4,800. The Trap: Candidates may apply debt-fund STCG (slab rate) by treating "hybrid" or "balanced" funds as automatically non-equity. The classification of a hybrid scheme as equity-oriented depends on its actual equity allocation per the scheme documents, not on the scheme name. Note: Always verify a hybrid scheme's equity-oriented status from the SID/AMC factsheet and use the current statutory rate from a tax source such as Series X-B before applying the 20% STCG figure in practice.
